description: Composite figure of two modalities for Fe30Mn11Al(x)C low-density steels with x = 0.6, 1.0, 1.2 and 1.5%C. Panels (a–d) are EBSD boundary/phase maps for (a) 0.6%C, (b) 1.0%C, (c) 1.2%C and (d) 1.5%C, each with a 200 µm scale bar; the shared legend defines black = boundaries with θ>15°, red = Twin boundary, green = BCC phase. Only (a) contains green BCC phase, present as thick elongated green bands crossing a finer austenite grain structure laced with red twin boundaries; (b–d) show no BCC phase and visibly coarser austenite grains with dense red twin boundaries, (d) additionally showing a few thick red bands. Panels (e–h) are dark-field TEM images of the κ phase for 0.6, 1.0, 1.2 and 1.5%C respectively, taken along [001]γ using a κ carbide reflection, each with an inset SAED pattern labelled (020)γ, (200)γ, (010)κ, (100)κ and the (000) transmitted spot; scale bars are 20 nm in (e,f) and 100 nm in (g,h). κ-carbide contrast coarsens from sub-resolution white speckle in (e,f) through resolvable particles in (g) to regular rectangular/square carbides in (h). The figure links ferrite-stabilised fine grains at 0.6%C to progressively coarser κ-carbides with increasing carbon.

subfigures.description: EBSD boundary/phase map, 200 µm scale bar, 0.6%C. Thick elongated green BCC phase bands traversing finer equiaxed austenite grains, with abundant red twin boundaries and black high-angle (θ>15°) boundaries. The only panel containing BCC phase.
EBSD map, 200 µm scale bar, 1.0%C. No green BCC phase; coarse austenite grains with many straight red twin boundaries inside the grains.
EBSD map, 200 µm scale bar, 1.2%C. No BCC phase; coarse austenite grains with abundant red twin boundaries.
EBSD map, 200 µm scale bar, 1.5%C. No BCC phase; coarse austenite grains with red twin boundaries plus several thicker red bands running across grains.

Dark-field TEM image, 20 nm scale bar, 0.6%C. Very fine, near-resolution-limit white speckle of κ-carbide contrast on a dark background; inset SAED pattern with faint κ spots indexed (010)κ and (100)κ alongside (020)γ, (200)γ and (000).
Dark-field TEM image, 20 nm scale bar, 1.0%C. Slightly coarser and brighter distributed κ-carbide speckle than (e); inset SAED with the same (0kk) reflections marked.
Dark-field TEM image, 100 nm scale bar, 1.2%C. Clearly resolvable bright κ-carbide particles (tens of nm) uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix; inset SAED with stronger κ reflections.
Dark-field TEM image, 100 nm scale bar, 1.5%C. Large, regularly shaped rectangular/square κ-carbide platelets arranged in a grid-like pattern; inset SAED pattern with the same γ/κ indices marked.

observations.observation: Panel (a) (0.6%C) is the only EBSD map containing green BCC-phase regions, which appear as thick elongated bands with long axes roughly parallel across a finer austenite grain structure.
Panels (b), (c) and (d) (1.0, 1.2 and 1.5%C) contain no green BCC-phase pixels — the mapped microstructures are single-phase austenite.
The shared legend at the bottom of the figure defines black lines as 'θ>15°', red lines as 'Twin boundary' and green colour as 'BCC phase'.
Scale bars printed in the figure: 200 µm in each of (a–d), 20 nm in (e) and (f), and 100 nm in (g) and (h).
The inset SAED patterns in (e–h) are indexed with (020)γ, (200)γ, (010)κ, (100)κ and the (000) transmitted spot, reflecting the [001]γ zone axis.

κ-carbide dark-field contrast in (e) and (f) consists of white speckle at or below the resolution limit, whereas (g) shows individually resolvable bright particles and (h) shows large regular rectangular/square platelets.
The caption states that (a–d) are EBSD maps showing grain and twin boundary (Σ3) arrangement together with BCC phase fraction for the 0.6–1.5%C samples.
The caption states that (e–h) are dark field TEM images of the κ phase taken along the [001]γ zone axis using one of the κ carbide diffraction spots shown in the inset SAED patterns.
The citing text states that in Fe30Mn11Al0.6C both FCC austenite and about 30 vol% BCC ferrite are present after solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching.

The citing text states that the average ferrite grain size in the 0.6%C steel is about 5.5 µm versus an austenite grain size of 7.3 µm, and that the austenite is significantly coarser in the 1.0–1.5%C (ferrite-free) samples, e.g. 22.5 µm in Fe30Mn11Al1.0C.
The citing text states that κ-carbides are smaller than 1 nm in the 0.6%C steel and have average diameters of about 2.0 nm (1.0%C), 25 nm (1.2%C) and 80 nm (1.5%C).
The citing text states that the orientation relationship between κ-carbides and austenite is (001)κ || (001)γ, with growth on {011} planes producing the rectangular shape seen in the 1.5%C steel.

The citing text states that the fractional twin boundary length f_Tw (twin boundary length divided by total length of boundaries with misorientation >15°) decreases from close to 60% at 0.6%C to 50% at 1.5%C (reported in Table 3, not in this figure).

The citing text gives two different κ-carbide sizes for the 1.5%C composition — 80 nm in the Fig. 3(e–h) discussion and 50 nm for Fe1.5C30Mn11Al in a later sentence — an internal inconsistency not resolvable from the image.

unreadable_items: SAED insets in (e–h) are rendered very small; the γ/κ spot indices are only partially readable at the supplied resolution and the exact match of spots to the green/orange annotation boxes relies on the caption
No numeric values (grain size, BCC fraction, κ-carbide diameter, f_Tw) are printed inside any panel; all such numbers come from the caption or citing text
Caption text for (e) is garbled ('(e 0.6%C') and the citing text refers to 'Fig. 2(e)' when discussing the 0.6%C dark field image
